data.ruling: The stock verifier's refutation stands, because INA228AIDGSR fails sourcing rule 4. JLCPCB's exact LCSC match is C2887910. It reads stockCount 0 and canPresaleNumber -254. The need is 5 boards (S7) x 2 placements, one INA228 for each shunt path (IOBoard.md:74, :112), which is 10. S4 sets the gate at 5 x 10 = 50 and never under 50, so the gate is 50, and 0 is under it. Rule 4 also fails any negative presale count, whatever the stock says. The part is not held: inventory-2026-09-25.csv has no row for C2887910 or INA228, so rule 6 does not apply. Digi-Key reads 0 in all three packagings with a 20-week lead time, so the second-vendor route of rule 5 fails too. The INA238 shares the footprint, but it has no charge or energy registers (V161, IOBoard.md:454). It therefore does not work in the same firmware configuration and is not a rule-5 alternate. The scope is the part: zero stock at both vendors and a negative presale count fail the gate at any need, so the part fails in both functions it fills. This agrees with the FU-2B2 and FU-2G R8 adjudicator rulings, which read presale -236 on 2026-10-02. The presale count is now -254. The lifecycle checks pass and are not part of the refutation: TI ACTIVE, Digi-Key Active, end_of_life false. The datasheet verifier's confirmation is not disputed. The owner's answer to V304 (2026-10-02) keeps the part as a fixed input. It records the unmet gate as a current limitation, gives T6 a stock exception, and has the stock read again before the order. Under Scope, a fixed input that fails a check is reported to the owner, not re-selected. V304 does not make rule 4 pass, so the refutation stands, it is reported to the owner, and no replacement candidate goes to new verifiers. The user request relayed to this run asks about V318/V319, the DC input range of 12 to 18 V. The owner answered it in V319 (2026-10-03). It has no bearing on this R8 stock ruling.
